elements.use_when: Use when a page has two or more parallel views of the same subject and the reader needs one at a time, such as a summary, the details and the raw data.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The tab list's accessible name, for example "Report sections".

elements.children: Direct-child <section> elements, each opening with an h2 to h6 heading as its first element child. The heading text becomes the tab label and stays in the panel, visually hidden. Without JavaScript the sections simply stack.
elements.example:
Summary

The 2.4 release shipped on schedule. Checkout latency improved, and one rollback was needed for the address form.

Timeline

Rollout started Tuesday at 09:00 UTC and reached every region by Wednesday at noon.

Follow-ups

  • Add a canary stage for the address form.
  • Alert on checkout p95 above 800 ms.

elements.use_when: Use when a small table of numbers is easier to read as a bar, line, area or donut chart and the finding can be stated in one sentence.

attributes.name: summary
attributes.description: One sentence stating the finding; it becomes the chart's accessible label.

attributes.name: x
attributes.description: Header of the column that holds the categories; defaults to the first column.

attributes.name: y
attributes.description: Comma-separated headers of the value columns; defaults to every other column.

attributes.name: stacked
attributes.description: Stack the series instead of drawing them side by side.

attributes.name: horizontal
attributes.description: Draw bars horizontally; applies to the bar type only.

attributes.name: data-from
attributes.description: Name of a field in the page's data file to chart instead of an inline table.

elements.children: A <table> whose <thead> has one <th> per column: the first column holds the categories and each other column is one series. Alternatively set data-from and omit the table. Optionally add a child <script type="application/json"> holding raw Chart.js options, which the theme guarantees override. At most 8 series are drawn.
elements.example:
MonthMedian minutes
June14
July12
August10
September9

elements.use_when: Use when a single headline number needs a label, a signed change and a definition of its period and denominator.

attributes.name: direction
attributes.description: Whether a rise is good or bad; colors the delta.

attributes.name: points
attributes.description: Two or more comma-separated numbers drawn as a decorative sparkline.

elements.children: Child elements marked with the slot attribute: slot="label", slot="value" and slot="definition" are required, and slot="delta" is optional. The delta's sign comes from its leading +, -, minus sign or digit. Adjacent q-stat elements form a responsive row.
elements.example: Weekly active users 58,200 +11.5% Distinct signed-in users per ISO week, versus the prior week. Checkout error rate 3.1% -0.3 pts Failed checkout attempts divided by all attempts, last 7 days. Median support wait 4m 20s +12s Time from first message to first human reply, last 7 days.

elements.use_when: Use when a table has more than a few rows and the reader will want to sort it, filter it or scroll it without the page scrolling sideways.

attributes.name: data-from
attributes.description: Name of a field in the page's data file to build the rows from.

elements.children: A <table> with a <thead>. Mark numeric columns with class="num" on their <th> so they sort by value. Clicking a header sorts ascending, then descending, then back to the authored order. With data-from, each <th> binds to the row field named by its data-key attribute, or else by its trimmed text.

elements.use_when: Use when events happen in order and the reader needs to see when each one occurred, such as an incident, a rollout or a project history.
elements.children: An <ol> whose every <li> holds a <time datetime> element followed by the event text. An <li> may carry data-tone set to neutral, success, warning or danger.
elements.example:
1. 09:02 Error rate on checkout crosses 2%.
  2. 09:10 Pager fires; incident declared.
  3. 09:31 Bad config identified in the 2.4 rollout.
  4. 09:44 Rollback complete; error rate back to baseline.

elements.use_when: Use when the reader should copy a command, config or code snippet exactly as written.

attributes.name: filename
attributes.description: File name shown in the header bar above the code; its extension picks the highlighting language when language is not set.

attributes.name: language
attributes.description: highlight.js language name or alias, such as yaml, json, bash or tsx; an unknown name shows plain text.

elements.children: A <pre> wrapping a <code> element with the text to copy. The code is highlighted by language, or else by the filename extension; with neither, or without JavaScript, it shows as plain text.

elements.use_when: Use when showing a code change for review, optionally with comments attached to specific new-side lines.
elements.children: A <pre> of unified diff text, followed by zero or more q-diff-note children. Each note names a file and a new-side line number that must appear in the diff. Code lines are highlighted by each file's extension. Without JavaScript the raw diff shows, then the notes as a list.
elements.example:
--- a/src/retry.py
+++ b/src/retry.py
@@ -10,6 +10,7 @@ def fetch(url):
     attempt = 0
-    while attempt < 3:
+    while attempt < MAX_ATTEMPTS:
         try:
             return get(url)
         except Timeout:
+            sleep(backoff(attempt))
             attempt += 1
The limit moves into a named constant so tests can lower it. Backoff runs before the counter changes, so the first retry waits the base delay.

elements.use_when: Use when attaching a review comment to a specific new-side line inside a q-diff.

attributes.name: file
attributes.description: Path as in the diff's +++ header, with the b/ prefix removed.

attributes.name: line
attributes.description: New-side line number the note sits under.

elements.example:
--- a/README.md
+++ b/README.md
@@ -1,2 +1,3 @@
 # Project
+Run `make test` before opening a pull request.
 Setup notes follow.
Name the exact command so contributors do not guess.

elements.use_when: Use when the reader should sort cards into columns, such as triage, prioritizing or planning, and hand the result back as Markdown.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: Board identifier; the saved layout is keyed by it.

elements.children: Direct-child <section> elements, each opening with an h2 to h6 heading and then a <ul> of <li> cards. A card's identity is its data-id attribute, or else its trimmed text.

  • Profile slow search queries

Next

elements.use_when: Use when several panels, stats or figures should sit side by side and stack on narrow screens, as on a dashboard.
elements.children: Any block children, usually q-panel or q-stat elements. They flow into equal columns: 1 at 700px and below, up to 2 from 701px, up to 4 from 1100px and up to 6 from 1800px (viewport widths). Give a child span="2" (q-panel) or data-span="2" (anything else) to take that many columns; a span never exceeds the columns in the row.
elements.example:
Checkout latency

The p95 fell from 410 ms to 310 ms after the cache change.

Error rate

3.1% of attempts failed in the last 7 days.

Open incidents

None.

elements.use_when: Use when one dashboard item, such as a chart, a table or a few stats, needs a title and a border of its own.

attributes.name: span
attributes.description: How many columns of an enclosing q-grid the panel spans; full takes the whole row.

elements.children: A heading (h2, h3 or h4) first: it is the panel's title. The body follows: paragraphs, q-chart, q-table, q-stat or any other content.
elements.example:
Weekly active users

58,200 distinct signed-in users in the last ISO week, up 11.5%.

elements.use_when: Use when a short aside, source or caveat belongs beside a sentence without interrupting it.
elements.children: Inline text placed inside a paragraph, right after the words it annotates. On a longform page of 1100px or wider it sits numbered in the right margin. Narrower, a numbered button in the text opens it in place. Without JavaScript, and in print, it reads inline in parentheses.
elements.example: Median build time fell to nine minutesMeasured on the main branch, excluding reruns. after the cache moved to the shared runner.

elements.use_when: Use when two or more options are judged against the same criteria and one of them is recommended.

attributes.name: recommended
attributes.description: The recommended option, counted from 1 across the option columns (the criteria column is not counted).

elements.children: A <table> whose first row is the header: the first cell names the criteria column and each other header cell is one option. Every later row is one criterion, with its name in the first cell. At 700px and below each option becomes its own block, the recommended one first. Wider, the table widens past the page column when the options do not fit. Without JavaScript the table scrolls inside its own box.
